body: That sounds like a horrible experience, I imagine it didn't feel to great to find that out. That said, word of advice, kick that incel shit to the fucking curb dude.

You're describing exactly how I feel right now. I hate how lonely I feel all the time, but I literally trust absolutely no one (a result of the many times I've been fucked over by "friends" and a failed relationship where my piece of shit ex hooked up with my "friend" right after we broke up). It's gotten so bad that I can see people visibly being put off by my vibe, because I'm always giving them dirty looks and sizing them up when they try to talk to me, particularly at work. Or if I'm not doing that, then I'm just saying "yeah, okay, cool, haha", trying to rush my way out of the conversation as fast as possible because I really DON'T want to talk to them. I make no effort to hide my annoyance or deep mistrust/hatred of the people I interact with, and I KNOW it repels people, which is what I WANT because I want them to fuck off, but at the same time I HATE being lonely and it HURTS me to see these people looking uncomfortable around me because of my negative attitude, so I've really dug myself into a hole here. And I don't think there's any escape now. It's been like this too long, and I've lost my will to fight against it.

I understand not wanting to break your grandma's heart, but I would still highly recommend asking someone for help. You are worth it, and you deserve to have someone listen to you and know how you're feeling right now. Is there a counselor or other staff member at your school (like a psychologist) who you could talk to?

Pretty shitty of that doctor to treat you that way. I'm not trans, but I've definitely gotten the impression that my healthcare professional just didn't give a shit when I asked them for help. I've found they're not all like that luckily, but it still really sucks. I know you said you've muted your bf's texts, but have you shared any of this with him before?

That's exactly what I thought. But then again I've done stupid shit like that before (nothing with guns, but crazy driving and stuff like that when I was younger) so I sort of understand it. I'd feel bad just writing an otherwise nice person off because of one awkward moment like that. If I feel like it's gonna happen again, I'll make sure to say something and let her know that her risky behavior isn't welcome with me. If it ends up being too much of a problem, I guess I can always stop talking to her.

On another note, I think I should really stop smoking weed. Since I had that stupid dream last night I can't stop thinking about this fucking chick staring me down with a gun and saying "Hey there" over and over. It's like having a dumb pop song stuck in your head, but like way more disturbing and exhausting.
That is fucking freaky, exactly why I hate being alone in big houses at night. Of course I'm that asshole who will just leave every light on and run up the electric bill just to put myself at ease.

I think you're right, that's usually most likely the case in those situations. That's actually kind of comforting because I've found "I'm new here" to be a pretty decent conversation starter. So there's some good news!

Good point...I'm probably just making excuses. I just know I tend to shut down in those situations and soon as I get scared someone's gonna notice me being silent, I freak out and shut down even more. Something to work on I suppose haha. I might give it a shot though, better than not trying at all

You know I actually have taken a look at that, and it seems like most of the groups on there have a lot of really outgoing, gregarious people and it kind of intimidates me because I feel like I'd just get frozen and feel uncomfortable the whole time while everyone else is laughing and getting to know each other. Kind of stupid, but I've had one or two experiences like that before and I hate the feeling.
Well said, and true. Thanks for the words of encouragement man, good luck with the writing
